title: Hammurabi's reign
dateNote: The Met gives ca. 1792–1750 BCE; the French Ministry gives 1792–1750. Treat these as conventional approximate endpoints; alternate absolute chronologies were not examined.

sentences.text: Hammurabi ruled Babylon in the conventionally dated period ca. 1792–1750 BCE.
The Met says he expanded Babylonian control in the south and unified much of Mesopotamia.
During his expansion, Hammurabi destroyed King Zimri-Lim's palace at Mari; the exact chronology and scale of destruction need closer specialist review.

relationships.label: Hammurabi's expansion and destruction of Zimri-Lim's palace

gaps: The cited pages do not compare chronological systems; keep the conventional dating qualifier and seek specialist chronology review.
No personal birth or death dates are inferred.
Babylon is a proposed dependency endpoint in this draft, not a confirmed existing collection record.

title: Mari
dateNote: No founding or end date is asserted in this calibration draft.

sentences.text: The French archaeological mission identifies Tell Hariri in the middle valley of the Syrian Euphrates as the site of ancient Mari.
Excavations found thousands of tablets in the Great Royal Palace, and the Met describes the palace archive as a source for contemporary political events.

gaps: No coordinates are proposed because an appropriately inspected coordinate source was not consulted.
Specific Mari archive texts, their dates and their contents were not examined; the general archive claim is limited.
The exact timing and effects of Hammurabi's attack on the city as a whole need closer review.
Null date bounds and point mean this city draft is not integration-ready.

title: Scribal education at Nippur
dateNote: The consulted University of Chicago page places the publication's subject in the Old Babylonian period but does not date House F's school activity more narrowly; no timeline interval is asserted.

sentences.text: A University of Chicago publication studies Old Babylonian education through House F at Nippur, which is widely believed to have been a scribal school.
The tablets found there document an educational curriculum, although the source page does not give a narrower date range for the activity discussed.

gaps: The exact dating and nature of House F's educational use need examination in the underlying excavation and specialist studies.
No point is asserted because coordinates were not researched and tied to a source claim.
Nippur is a proposed dependency endpoint in this draft, not a confirmed existing collection record. Null date bounds and point mean this draft is not integration-ready.
